blocks.text: 2 Samuel 24 contains 25 verses. It opens with: And again the anger of Jehovah was kindled against Israel, and he moved David against them, saying, Go, number Israel and Judah. It concludes with: And David built there an altar unto Jehovah, and offered burnt-offerings and peace-offerings. So Jehovah was entreated for the land, and the plague was stayed from Israel. Supplied contextual evidence for this passage adds: Second Samuel attributes the census incitement to the LORD's anger, whereas First Chronicles attributes it to an adversary; harmonizing, developmental, and distinct-source explanations remain debated. Second Samuel moves from David's accession and kingdom consolidation through ark and dynasty promise to royal abuse, household violence, rebellion, grief, and a four-part closing appendix.
